topics.title: Microsoft Foundry documentation
topics.summary: The AI app and agent factory - build, optimize, and govern AI apps and agents at scale.

topics.title: Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Foundry
topics.summary: Microsoft Agent 365 is Microsoft's enterprise control plane for AI agents. It treats agents as first-class Microsoft Entra identities through Entra Agent ID. This identity model lets organizations apply authentication, authorization, and lifecycle governance directly to agent identity objects.

topics.title: Agent identity concepts in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: An agent identity is a specialized identity type in Microsoft Entra ID that's designed specifically for AI agents. It provides a standardized framework for governing, authenticating, and authorizing AI agents across Microsoft services.

topics.title: What is the agent optimizer?
topics.summary: The agent optimizer in Foundry Agent Service automatically improves prompt agents and hosted agents by evaluating their behavior and generating better configurations. Depending on the agent type, these configurations can include improved instructions, skills, tool descriptions, and model selection.

topics.title: Durable state store for Microsoft Foundry hosted agents
topics.summary: The durable state store for Microsoft Foundry hosted agents provides server-backed key-value storage for JSON data that must persist when an agent container crashes, restarts, or is evicted after an idle period.

topics.title: Deep dive into Foundry Agent Service networking
topics.summary: When you run Microsoft Foundry Agent Service with a bring-your-own virtual network (VNet), you're responsible for sizing the delegated subnet, planning IP allocation, and understanding how agent traffic flows through the platform.

topics.title: Agent development lifecycle
topics.summary: The agent development lifecycle in Microsoft Foundry spans from initial creation through production monitoring. At the core of every agent is a model from the Foundry model catalog that drives reasoning and response generation.

topics.summary: Foundry IQ enables agents to access, process, and act on knowledge from anywhere.

topics.title: Hosted agent runtime contract
topics.summary: A hosted agent is a container that fulfills a specific runtime contract with the Microsoft Foundry platform. This reference describes what the platform expects from your container and how the SDK adapter packages help you meet those requirements.

topics.title: Hosted agent permissions reference
topics.summary: When working with Hosted agents in Microsoft Foundry, it's important to understand the various permissions involved. There are several classes of permissions involved in Hosted agent development, spanning the Azure Resource Manager control plane and the Foundry data plane:

topics.title: What are hosted agents?
topics.summary: When you build agentic applications by using open-source frameworks, you typically manage many cross-cutting concerns: containerization, web server setup, security, memory persistence, scaling, instrumentation, and version rollbacks. These tasks become even more challenging in heterogeneous cloud environments.

topics.title: Identity and access overview for Foundry Agent Service
topics.summary: Identity and access decisions in Agent Service span three boundaries: management access to Foundry resources, caller access to the agent endpoint, and agent access to downstream tools or resources. Each boundary has its own authentication and authorization configuration.

topics.title: Foundry Agent Service limits, quotas, and regional support
topics.summary: Foundry Agent Service enforces quotas and limits on agent artifacts, file uploads, messages, and tool registrations. Understanding these limits helps you design applications that scale without hitting service boundaries.

topics.title: Resilience for long-running Microsoft Foundry hosted agents
topics.summary: Long-running hosted agents can keep working after the request that started them disconnects. They can also recover after their hosting process stops unexpectedly. Foundry Agent Service and the AgentServer SDKs provide durable work identity, persisted inputs, lease-based recovery, and stream replay.

topics.title: What are prompt agents?
topics.summary: Prompt agents in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service are declaratively defined agents for text interactions. You configure a model, instructions, and tools, and Foundry runs the agent for you. You don't write or operate the orchestration code, package a container, or manage compute.

topics.title: Routines in Foundry Agent Service
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry provides routines in Foundry Agent Service that run an agent automatically when a defined trigger fires. Use a routine when you want a project-native way to say, "When a specific time, schedule, or event occurs, invoke this agent."

topics.title: Build with agents, conversations, and responses
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service uses three core runtime components— agents , conversations , and responses —to power stateful, multi-turn interactions. An agent uses a model from the Foundry model catalog, along with instructions and tools. A conversation persists history across turns.

topics.title: What is Toolbox in Foundry?
topics.summary: As organizations adopt AI agents, managing tools across agents can become increasingly complex. Agents often connect directly to tools, APIs, MCP servers, and other services, requiring separate configuration, authentication, and governance for each implementation.

topics.title: What is Toolbox in Foundry?
topics.summary: As organizations adopt AI agents, managing tools across agents can become increasingly complex. Agents often connect directly to tools, APIs, MCP servers, and other services, requiring separate configuration, authentication, and governance for each implementation.

topics.title: User delegation for tools in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Client user delegation lets an agent access a downstream tool or resource in the context of a signed-in user represented by the client that calls the agent.

topics.title: Vector stores for file search
topics.summary: Vector store objects give the file search tool the ability to search your files. Adding a file to a vector store provides the agent's Foundry model with knowledge beyond its training data. The service parses, chunks, embeds, and indexes the file so the tool can run both keyword and semantic search.

topics.title: Best practices for voice-based agents
topics.summary: This article shows the design, security, and operational practices that matter most when you build, test, secure, and release a voice-based agent in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service.

topics.title: Voice agent tracing, monitoring, and evaluation
topics.summary: Voice-based agents use the same observability and evaluation stack as other agents in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service. They use the same Application Insights connection, OpenTelemetry data, tracing tools, monitoring dashboard, and transcript-based evaluators.

topics.title: Pricing for voice-based agents
topics.summary: A voice-based agent bills differently from a text agent because audio, not text, is the main input and output. A single minute of conversation produces far more tokens than a minute of typing, and the way you host the model changes which meter the usage lands on.

topics.title: What is Foundry IQ?
topics.summary: Azure AI Search is now Foundry IQ. This article explains how agents use its higher-level knowledge retrieval APIs through knowledge bases, knowledge sources, and agentic retrieval. For the full range of service capabilities, see the service overview.

topics.summary: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service support real-time voice workloads through the invocations ws WebSocket protocol. This article shows you how to choose a voice framework, expose the WebSocket endpoint from your container, and connect a client.

topics.title: Configure environment variables for a hosted agent
topics.summary: Configure environment variables for your hosted agent by defining where values belong in azure.yaml , what the Microsoft Foundry platform provides automatically, and how azd environment integration works. You also learn how to add custom variables and handle local development secrets.

topics.title: Configure a voice agent
topics.summary: A voice-based agent in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service is an agent whose kind is voice . Its definition holds everything the service needs to run a spoken conversation: which model serves the session, what the agent says first, how it listens, how it sounds, and which tools it can call.

topics.title: Connect models to Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
topics.summary: Foundry Agent Service lets you connect models that are already available through another Microsoft Foundry resource, an Azure OpenAI resource, an AI gateway, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. You can then use a connected model when you create an agent.

topics.title: Create an evaluation dataset and evaluators
topics.summary: The agent optimizer evaluates your agent against a dataset - a collection of tasks - scored by evaluators . You can generate both automatically from the CLI or create a dataset manually for full control.

topics.title: Deploy a hosted agent
topics.summary: This article shows you how to deploy a containerized agent to Foundry Agent Service by using the Azure Developer CLI ( azd ), the Python, .NET, or JavaScript/TypeScript SDK, or the REST API. Choose a deployment method by using the selector at the top of the article.

topics.title: Deploy a hosted agent from source code
topics.summary: This article shows you how to deploy a Hosted agent in Foundry Agent Service from Python or .NET source code, without building or pushing a container image. You upload a .zip of your code (and optionally your dependencies), and Agent Service either runs it as-is or builds your dependencies for you in the cloud.

topics.title: Enable incoming A2A on a Foundry agent
topics.summary: You can expose your Foundry Agent Service agent as an Agent2Agent (A2A) endpoint so that other agents can discover and call it through the A2A protocol. When incoming A2A is enabled, Foundry publishes an agent card for your agent and accepts inbound A2A requests from external callers.

topics.summary: Use Azure Policy to require egress configurations that meet your organization's standards. Audit configurations before enforcement, then deny noncompliant changes without relying on each developer to apply the same conventions.

topics.title: Invoke a hosted agent with the Azure Developer CLI
topics.summary: Use azd ai agent invoke to send messages to your agent, either the deployed version in Microsoft Foundry or a locally running instance. You learn how to choose an agent, use direct endpoints, manage sessions, send files, pin versions, and inspect raw responses.

topics.title: Manage hosted agents
topics.summary: This article shows you how to manage Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service. After you deploy a Hosted agent, you can view its status, create new versions, select the version served by the agent endpoint, monitor logs, and delete agents when they're no longer needed.

topics.title: Manage hosted agent session compute
topics.summary: Use the preview session compute APIs in Microsoft Foundry to inspect the environment that runs your hosted agent session. You can start stopped compute, change its idle timeout, read its network settings, and stream container logs.

topics.title: Manage hosted agent sessions
topics.summary: This article shows you how to manage sessions for hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service. A session is a stateful, isolated workload (for example, one user's chat) with backing sandbox compute.

topics.title: Manage state for long-running agents
topics.summary: A long-running hosted agent recovers from crashes only if its progress is durable. This article shows how to keep progress markers and checkpoints in the Foundry state store, and how to back a framework checkpointer so framework-level recovery survives restarts.

topics.title: Migrate to the new agents developer experience
topics.summary: A migration tool is available to help automate migration from the Assistants API to Agents.

topics.title: Migrate from Voice Live with Foundry Agent Service to Microsoft Foundry voice agents
topics.summary: Migrate an existing Voice Live with Foundry Agent Service integration to a voice-based prompt agent in Microsoft Foundry. First, compare the architectures and choose how to preserve your tools and business logic. Then move the configuration, update the WebSocket client, and test responsiveness before switching traffic.

topics.title: Monitor hosted agent logs with the Azure Developer CLI
topics.summary: Stream and inspect logs from your deployed Microsoft Foundry hosted agent for troubleshooting and observability. You learn how to view console logs, stream in real time, inspect system events, filter by session, and recognize common log patterns.

topics.title: Optimize agent instructions, skills, tools, and models
topics.summary: The agent optimizer improves four aspects of your hosted agent: instructions , skills , tools , and model selection . It automatically detects which of these targets to optimize from your agent's baseline configuration.

topics.title: Optimize voice agent instructions
topics.summary: Instructions written for a text chat agent rarely work perfectly in a voice agent. A human caller can't skim a numbered list, can't see a table, and won't wait through a paragraph to hear an answer. A good text reply often makes a spoken reply too long, too formal, and easy to interrupt.

topics.title: Publish agents to Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Teams in the Foundry portal
topics.summary: After you build and test an agent, you often want to share it with others in the surfaces where they already work. When you publish a Microsoft Foundry agent to Microsoft Copilot and Teams, you and others can interact with and discover your agent through the Microsoft Copilot and Teams UI.

topics.title: Publish agents to Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Teams by using the REST API
topics.summary: This article shows how to publish a Microsoft Foundry agent to Microsoft Copilot and Teams by using the REST API without creating a separate Azure Bot Service resource. You can follow it for any project, whether or not public network access is disabled:

topics.title: Register external agents for observability and evaluation
topics.summary: When you use external agents with other Microsoft products and services, you must read all relevant documentation for such products and services and understand related risks and compliance considerations.

topics.title: Run a hosted agent locally with the Azure Developer CLI
topics.summary: Use azd ai agent run to start your Microsoft Foundry hosted agent on your local machine and azd ai agent invoke --local to test it without deploying to Azure. You also learn how to set ports, choose an agent in a multi-agent project, override startup commands, and pass local runtime secrets.

topics.title: Connect to an A2A agent endpoint from Foundry Agent Service
topics.summary: You can extend the capabilities of your Microsoft Foundry agent by connecting to a remote Agent2Agent (A2A) endpoint that supports the A2A protocol. The A2A tool enables agent-to-agent communication through a standardized protocol, allowing your Foundry agent to exchange context and collaborate with external agents.

topics.title: Connect a Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search) index to Foundry agents
topics.summary: Ground your Foundry agent's responses in your proprietary content by connecting it to a Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search) index. The Foundry IQ tool retrieves indexed documents so the Foundry model powering the agent can generate answers with inline citations, enabling accurate, source-backed responses.

topics.title: Connect Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to an agent
topics.summary: Azure Speech in Foundry Tools lets your agent convert speech to text and generate speech audio from text. You connect the tool by adding a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to your agent in Foundry Agent Service.

topics.title: Use Azure Functions with Foundry Agent Service
topics.summary: Learn how to integrate Azure Functions with Microsoft Foundry agents by using a queue-based tool approach. This article shows you how to build custom serverless tools that an agent's Foundry model can call asynchronously through Azure Queue storage.

topics.title: What is Browser automation tool?
topics.summary: Browser automation tool is a generally available (GA) service that lets Microsoft Foundry agents navigate websites, read information, and interact with web applications through a managed remote browser.

topics.title: Code Interpreter tool for Microsoft Foundry agents
topics.summary: Code Interpreter enables a Microsoft Foundry agent to run Python code in a sandboxed execution environment. The agent's Foundry model writes and executes code for data analysis, chart generation, and iterative problem-solving tasks.

topics.title: Use the computer use tool in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
topics.summary: The computer use tool is generally available and enables agents to interact with browsers and desktop applications through their user interfaces. The model interprets screenshots and proposes actions such as clicking, typing, and scrolling.

topics.title: File search tool for agents
topics.summary: Use the file search tool to ground Microsoft Foundry agents in your own data. With file search, agents can retrieve relevant information from your documents and use it to generate more accurate, context-aware responses, augmenting agents with knowledge such as proprietary product information or user-provided documents.

topics.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry agents support function calling, which lets you extend agents with custom capabilities. Define a function with its name, parameters, and description, and the agent's Foundry model can request your app to call it. Your app executes the function and returns the output.

topics.title: Govern MCP tools by using a gateway
topics.summary: Control how your agents access external tools by routing Model Context Protocol (MCP) traffic through either the new AI Gateway or the Azure API Management service. Azure API Management supports MCP routes in supported classic (v1) and v2 service tiers.

topics.title: Use the image generation tool (preview)
topics.summary: The image generation tool in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service generates images from text prompts in conversations and multistep workflows. The agent's Foundry model orchestrates the image generation request and returns base64-encoded output that you can save to a file.

topics.title: Connect agents to Model Context Protocol servers
topics.summary: Connect your Foundry agents to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers by using the MCP tool. This connection extends agent capabilities with external tools and data sources.

topics.title: Monitor toolbox usage in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Use the Monitor dashboard in Microsoft Foundry to see how agents use a toolbox and identify calls that need investigation. Review tool selection, skill usage, agent-to-agent (A2A) calls, and errors for a specific toolbox version.

topics.title: Connect agents to OpenAPI tools
topics.summary: Connect your Microsoft Foundry agents to external APIs using OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 specifications. The Foundry model powering your agent can call external services, retrieve real-time data, and extend its capabilities beyond built-in functions.

topics.summary: Toolbox authentication in Microsoft Foundry determines how tools authenticate to downstream services.

topics.title: Create and manage a toolbox in Foundry
topics.summary: When you connect to non-Foundry tools, you might incur costs and data might be sent outside Foundry's compliance boundary and processed according to the applicable terms and data handling policies. See the tool's documentation to learn how to manage access to the tool.

topics.title: Use a toolbox with a hosted agent
topics.summary: A hosted agent runs your code in Foundry Agent Service. In this article, you connect that code to a toolbox so the agent discovers and calls the toolbox tools through one Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint.

topics.title: Web grounding tools overview
topics.summary: Web grounding tools in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service connect your agents to real-time public web data, overcoming the knowledge cutoff of the agent's Foundry model. For example, you can ask questions such as "what is the top AI news today" and receive current, cited answers.

topics.summary: A routine is a named automation rule that triggers an agent on a schedule, at a specific time, or in response to an external event. You define what fires the routine (the trigger ) and what agent to invoke (the action ).

topics.summary: This article explains how the voice-based channels experience differs from standard agent application and Microsoft Teams app publishing. In the Foundry portal, use the voice-based Channels tab to share a browser preview or connect a phone number.

topics.title: Integrate telephony channels with a voice agent
topics.summary: Use Teams Phone extensibility (TPE) or Twilio to connect a phone number to your Microsoft Foundry voice agent. Receive inbound calls and place outbound calls through the call-job API.

topics.title: Agents in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Foundry Agent Service is a managed platform for building, deploying, and scaling AI agents. Build with any framework, any supported model from the Foundry model catalog, and a single entry point for model inference and tools.

topics.title: Quickstart: Create a prompt agent
topics.summary: In this quickstart, you create a prompt agent in Foundry Agent Service and have a conversation with it. A prompt agent is a declaratively defined agent that combines a model from the Foundry model catalog, instructions, tools, and natural language prompts to drive behavior.

topics.title: Quickstart: Create a voice-based prompt agent
topics.summary: In this quickstart, you create a voice-based prompt agent, open a live session, complete a spoken turn, and read the conversation back. Foundry Agent Service manages the voice orchestration, so you don't host a speech pipeline of your own.

topics.title: Quickstart: Deploy your own code as a hosted agent

topics.title: Quickstart: Hosted agent CI/CD templates
topics.summary: You can establish a Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline for a hosted agent in Microsoft Foundry project. This quickstart helps enterprise hosted agent developers validate code changes after they update agent source code.

topics.title: What is Microsoft Foundry (classic) portal?
topics.summary: This article covers the Foundry (classic) portal and APIs. For the current platform experience, see What is Microsoft Foundry?.

topics.title: AI Red Teaming Agent
topics.summary: The AI Red Teaming Agent is a powerful tool designed to help organizations proactively find safety risks associated with generative AI systems during design and development of generative AI models and applications.

topics.title: Microsoft Foundry architecture
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry organizes AI workloads through a layered architecture: a top-level Foundry resource for governance, projects for development isolation, and connected Azure services for storage, search, and secrets management.

topics.title: Authentication and authorization in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Authentication and authorization in Microsoft Foundry control how principals prove identity and gain permission to perform operations. Foundry divides operations into control plane (resource management) and data plane (runtime usage), each with its own authentication and role-based access control (RBAC) surface.

topics.title: Billing concepts for Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry bills you for the underlying Azure services and models that you use. How each charge accrues depends on its billing model, such as pay-as-you-go or provisioned throughput. For models, it also depends on whether Azure or a partner sells the model.

topics.title: Microsoft Foundry capability reference

topics.title: Microsoft Foundry Notification Center
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry Notification Center centralizes all important observability alerts and notifications for your AI agents, models, and projects. Previously, developers had to manually monitor multiple siloed systems and configure Azure Monitor alerts to catch agent issues.

topics.title: Evaluation in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Evaluation helps you measure the quality, safety, and reliability of models and agents throughout development and production. In Microsoft Foundry, you can evaluate existing outputs in a test dataset, generate responses from a model or agent by using test inputs, or evaluate production traces.

topics.title: Rate limits, region support, and enterprise features for evaluation
topics.summary: This article provides an overview of which regions support AI-assisted evaluators, the rate limits that apply to evaluation runs, how to configure virtual network support for network isolation, and using your own storage account to run evaluations.

topics.title: Overview of Microsoft Foundry Models
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry Models is your one-stop destination for discovering, evaluating, and deploying powerful AI models. Whether you're building a custom copilot, an agent, enhancing an existing application, or exploring new AI capabilities, Foundry Models has you covered.

topics.title: Microsoft Foundry portal general availability overview
topics.summary: The new Microsoft Foundry portal is generally available (GA). This milestone marks a shift from pilot-focused usage to secure, reliable, enterprise-ready production usage for core scenarios.

topics.title: Instant access to models in Microsoft Foundry (preview)
topics.summary: Instant access to models lets you call any supported model by name — no deployment required. Create a Foundry project, start coding, and use any available model immediately.

topics.title: Cost and FinOps in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: FinOps is the practice of managing cloud spending as a shared job for engineering, finance, and business teams. Microsoft Foundry supports that practice for AI workloads.

topics.title: Managed compute in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Managed compute is a deployment type in Microsoft Foundry that hosts open-source models on dedicated GPU capacity without requiring you to provision virtual machines, operate a Kubernetes cluster, build container images, or own a model-serving runtime.

topics.title: Model leaderboards in Microsoft Foundry portal (preview)
topics.summary: Items marked preview in this article are currently in preview. This preview is provided without a service-level agreement, and Microsoft doesn't recommend it for production workloads. Certain features might not be supported or might have constrained capabilities.

topics.title: Monitoring concepts for managed compute
topics.summary: Monitoring a managed compute deployment combines a quick operational view in the Microsoft Foundry portal with deeper analysis through Azure Monitor metrics. These metrics are separate from the cost data for the deployment.

topics.title: Observability in generative AI
topics.summary: The AI application lifecycle requires robust evaluation frameworks to ensure AI systems deliver accurate, relevant, and reliable outputs. Without rigorous assessment, AI systems risk generating responses that are inaccurate, inconsistent, poorly grounded, or potentially harmful.

topics.title: Microsoft Foundry rollout across my organization
topics.summary: A structured deployment plan helps you avoid security gaps, cost overruns, and access sprawl when you adopt Microsoft Foundry at scale. Use this guide to define workload boundaries, choose a resource topology, and establish governance for self-serve teams.

topics.title: Role-based access control for Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: RBAC roles apply when you authenticate using Microsoft Entra ID. If you use key-based authentication instead, the key grants full access without role restrictions. Microsoft recommends using Entra ID authentication for improved security and granular access control.

topics.title: Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and indexes
topics.summary: Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is a pattern that combines search with large language models (LLMs) so responses are grounded in your data. This article explains how RAG works in Microsoft Foundry, what role indexes play, and how agentic retrieval changes classic RAG patterns.

topics.title: Microsoft Foundry risk and safety evaluations Transparency Note
topics.summary: An AI system includes not only the technology, but also the people who will use it, the people who will be affected by it, and the environment in which it's deployed.

topics.title: Configure Azure AI Gateway in your Foundry resources
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry can consume models through either Azure AI Gateway or Azure API Management. These options are distinct resource types with separate management experiences. Use this article to choose an option and make gateway-managed models and tools available to Foundry projects.

topics.title: Govern tools in Microsoft Foundry (preview)
topics.summary: Use Azure Policy in Microsoft Foundry to govern saved toolbox configurations and prompt agents without the Microsoft Copilot harness. Use project tool controls to restrict runtime tool use. Keep their allow lists aligned, and verify saving and running separately.

topics.title: Manage agents at scale in Microsoft Foundry Control Plane
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry Control Plane provides centralized management and observability for agents that run across supported platforms and infrastructures. By using Foundry Control Plane, you can manage agents that are distributed across multiple projects within a subscription.

topics.title: Monitor AI governance and compliance in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Use Compliance in Microsoft Foundry to review the policies and protections that apply to your agents, models, and tools. Identify policy violations, affected assets, and governance gaps that need attention.

topics.title: Monitor your agent fleet in Microsoft Foundry (preview)
topics.summary: To see the activity, health, and cost of the agents and models across an Azure subscription in one place, go to Manage Fleet in the Microsoft Foundry portal. The Fleet overview page summarizes the scope and date range that you select.

topics.title: Monitor agent and model operations in Microsoft Foundry (preview)
topics.summary: To see how often the agents and models in an Azure subscription run, and how reliably, go to Manage Operations in the Microsoft Foundry portal. The Operations page shows agent runs, model requests, tool calls, tokens, errors, and latency for the scope and date range that you select.

topics.title: Monitor agent health and performance across your fleet
topics.summary: As your organization scales from isolated copilots to autonomous multi-agent fleets, maintaining visibility and control becomes critical. Microsoft Foundry Control Plane provides a unified command center where you can monitor all agents, models, and tools across your enterprise from build to production.

topics.title: Foundry governance
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry governance, previously known as Foundry Control Plane, is the centralized management experience for enterprise AI fleets.

topics.title: Deploy fine-tuned models in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Deploy your fine-tuned model in the Microsoft Foundry portal with Serverless or Managed Compute. Start with a fine-tuned model that's ready for deployment.

topics.title: Fine-tune a model with supervised fine-tuning in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Prepare your data and create a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) job with Managed Training in Microsoft Foundry. For method comparisons and training concepts, see the fine-tuning overview.

topics.title: Training in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Training in Microsoft Foundry adapts a pretrained model to your task with task-specific data. It adjusts the model's weights rather than adding examples to each prompt. You build on the model's existing capabilities without training a model from scratch.

topics.title: Claude Consumption Units (CCU) billing in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: This article explains how Claude models from Anthropic are billed in Microsoft Foundry. Claude models use a billing unit called the Claude Consumption Unit (CCU) , which is the same construct Anthropic uses across its other supported cloud platforms.

topics.title: Compare hosting options for Claude models in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry offers Claude models in two hosting configurations: Hosted on Azure and Hosted on Anthropic infrastructure . This article outlines how the various aspects are impacted by the hosting option you choose.

topics.summary: Anthropic's Claude models bring advanced conversational AI capabilities to Microsoft Foundry, enabling you to build intelligent applications with state-of-the-art language understanding and generation. Claude models excel at complex reasoning, code generation, and multimodal tasks including image analysis.

topics.title: Microsoft Foundry Models quotas and limits
topics.summary: This article provides a quick reference and detailed description of the quotas and limits for Foundry Models sold by Azure. For quotas and limits specific to the Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models, see Quotas and limits in Azure OpenAI.

topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry provides safety and security guardrails that you can apply to core models and agents. Agent guardrails for content safety in Foundry Agent Service are in preview. Guardrails consist of a set of controls.

topics.title: How to configure guardrails and controls in Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Learn to create, configure, and manage guardrails for your model deployments and agents in Microsoft Foundry using the Foundry portal or the REST API.

topics.title: Govern agent kinds and hosted agent container images
topics.summary: Use built-in Azure Policy definitions to control which agent kinds your organization permits and which container images hosted agents can use in Microsoft Foundry. Assign the policies at your governance scope, configure their parameters, and validate the resulting restrictions before enforcing them in production.

topics.summary: Use a private endpoint to secure communication. This article describes how to establish a private connection to your Foundry account and projects using a private endpoint.

topics.summary: Cost controls let you set a spending or token budget for a Foundry resource or a project, and send alerts or block requests as usage approaches it. In this article, you create, monitor, edit, and delete cost controls in the Microsoft Foundry portal, and you create them programmatically with the REST API.

topics.title: Create a project for Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: Use this article to create a project in Microsoft Foundry and confirm that your environment is ready. Projects organize agents, evaluations, and files as you build stateful apps and explore new ideas.

topics.title: Create an agent with Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code
topics.summary: Use Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code to configure a prompt agent or develop a code-based hosted agent. Choose a creation route based on whether instructions and supported tools meet your needs, or you need custom runtime logic.

topics.title: Create a prompt agent with Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code
topics.summary: Use Agent Builder in Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code to configure a prompt agent's model, instructions, and tools. Test the agent in the playground, save changes as versions, and generate client code to call it from an application.

topics.title: Host Microsoft Agent Framework agents as Foundry hosted agents
topics.summary: Use the Microsoft Agent Framework hosting packages to expose an Agent Framework agent through the protocols for Foundry hosted agents. The hosting packages let you keep your agent logic in code while Foundry manages the hosted runtime, sessions, scale, identity, and protocol endpoints.

topics.title: Prepare your development environment
topics.summary: Prepare your development environment to build with Microsoft Foundry. You need a supported programming language, Git, and the Foundry developer tools that fit your workflow.

topics.summary: Install Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code from the Visual Studio Marketplace or the Extensions view. When you finish, the Foundry Toolkit view is available in Visual Studio Code.

topics.summary: Use the langchain-azure-ai package as the entry point for building LangChain and LangGraph applications with Microsoft Foundry capabilities. topics.title: Host LangGraph agents as Foundry hosted agents
topics.summary: Use langchain-azure-ai[hosting] to expose a compiled LangGraph graph as a Microsoft Foundry hosted agent. This integration lets you keep your LangChain and LangGraph agent logic in code while Foundry manages the hosted runtime, sessions, scale, identity, and protocol endpoints.

topics.summary: Agent Inspector in Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code lets you send requests to a local agent, inspect model and tool activity, and debug your code. Use it to investigate unexpected responses before you deploy a change.

topics.summary: Use Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code to work with existing declarative workflows and prepare them for migration. You can test a saved workflow, edit its exported YAML, and use GitHub Copilot to help convert the definition to Microsoft Agent Framework code.

topics.summary: Use Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code to create a code-based workflow from a Microsoft Agent Framework sample. Run it locally with Agent Inspector, then deploy its source code to Foundry Agent Service as a hosted agent. You maintain the code and its dependencies.

topics.title: Collect and inspect traces in Microsoft Foundry Toolkit
topics.summary: Use Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code to collect local traces or view telemetry for agents deployed to Microsoft Foundry. topics.summary: This article provides guidance on migrating your applications from the now-retired Azure AI Inference SDK to the OpenAI SDK. topics.summary: Quota provides the flexibility to actively manage the allocation of rate limits across the deployments within your subscription. Azure assigns quota per subscription, per region, and per model in units of tokens per minute (TPM).

topics.summary: If you don't set up a Key Vault connection, Microsoft Foundry stores connection details in a Microsoft-managed Key Vault outside your subscription. topics.title: What is model router?
topics.summary: Model router in Microsoft Foundry gives you frontier-level quality at a lower cost. It's a routing model, trained by Microsoft on billions of interactions, that judges how demanding each request is and sends it to the model best suited to answer it. Simple prompts go to small, fast models.

topics.title: Generate embeddings with Azure OpenAI
topics.summary: An embedding is a vector of floating-point numbers that represents the semantic meaning of text. Similar text produces vectors that are close together, which makes embeddings useful for vector search, recommendations, classification, and clustering.

While Microsoft strives to make all features available in all regions where Microsoft Foundry is supported at the same time, feature availability might vary by region.

topics.title: Responsible AI for Microsoft Foundry
topics.summary: This article provides an overview of the resources for building and deploying trustworthy AI agents. This includes end-to end security, observability, and governance with controls and checkpoints at all stages of the agent lifecycle.

topics.title: Quickstart: Set up Microsoft Foundry resources
topics.summary: In this quickstart, you create a Microsoft Foundry project and deploy a model. If you're managing a team, you also grant access to team members. After you complete these steps, you or your team can start building AI applications using the deployed model.

topics.title: What is Microsoft Foundry?
topics.summary: Microsoft Foundry unifies agents, models, and tools under a single management grouping with built-in enterprise-readiness capabilities including tracing, monitoring, evaluations, and customizable enterprise setup configurations.
